name: Yale Center for British Art
notes: Louis Kahn's Yale Center for British Art (1977) on Chapel Street, New Haven: a four-storey block of ten by six 20-foot bays, its exposed concrete frame filled with matte (pewter) stainless-steel panels (drawn in the darker grey) and glass where the photographs of it usually show it — shop fronts along Chapel Street at street level, a few gallery windows higher up; the entrance is the open corner bay at Chapel and High Streets; the roof is covered with rows of skylights over the top-floor galleries. Set on the street grid's bearing from the OpenStreetMap ground, rasterised in rows. Bay size and storey count from general knowledge; the floor heights and which bays are glazed are approximate. No photographs were available.
